Risk officer read: this is a weak setup for a buy. The coin is ORGANIC by class, but the curve data is mixed. Bundle share is 57% and completer share 55%, which points to heavy coordinated early activity, not clean retail flow. The last 15 minutes show sells (502 SOL) nearly matching buys (530 SOL), net flow of only +27 SOL, and the coin is already 49% off its 30-minute high after a 145% run. Pool depth of 121 SOL is thin enough that a $20 round trip with 1.4-5% costs plus impact is a meaningful drag.

If the desk insists on buying: $5 ticket, 25% hard stop, 30-minute max hold.

Refuse any size if the bundle/completer concentration is confirmed as operator-driven, if sell pressure outpaces buys again on the next check, or if the drawdown deepens past 50% without stabilization. My default is to skip.
memos.scout:
Case for buying "snowball" now, as honestly as the brief allows:

The strongest signal is the last 15 minutes: 847 buyers and $122k volume, with a 32% return and only ~$27 SOL net inflow, meaning the tape is two-sided and turnover is high rather than one-way. The coin is alive at 30.7 minutes, with 1,016 buyers and no airdrop dump. Top-3 holder concentration is low (7.7%) and the top-5 buyer share in the first two minutes after graduation is 18.7%, which argues against a single whale carrying the chart. It also sits 145% above its 30-minute-ago price.

The case has real holes. Price is 49% off its 30-minute high, the curve shows 57% bundle share and 55% of activity from completers, and the first two minutes saw sells slightly exceeding buys. Those point to sophisticated bundling and early exit liquidity, not clean organic demand. Pool depth of 121 SOL means a $20 round trip will cost near the high end of the fee range.

Verdict: the best case is that momentum persists for 30-60 minutes, but the drawdown and bundle profile make that a coin flip at best against a roughly 20% base-rate loss. Only a weak case for buying now; skipping is defensible.
memos.skeptic: Most likely loss: insider distribution after a 145% run. The curve shows bundle_share at 57% and completer_share at 55%, so most early supply sits with bundled wallets, and the top-3 holder share of 7.7% looks clean only because the bundles are spread across wallets. The first 2 minutes after graduation show a sell-to-buy ratio of 1.08 (more SOL sold than bought) and a launch bot present. The last 15 minutes are net negative flow: buys of 529.5 SOL against sells of 502.7 SOL, with sellers (682) outnumbering the buyer count gain. Price is already 49% off its 30-minute high. With a 1.4-5.1% round-trip cost and a 120 SOL pool, a further 10% leg down wipes any bounce. Skip.
